title: They thought it was coincidence.
paragraphs: They thought it was coincidence.

Wrong place.
Wrong time.
Three crosses… just bad luck.
But heaven doesn’t deal in accidents.

Jesus didn’t just die between two criminals.
He died exactly where He chose to be.
Because that middle cross?
It was yours.
Two men. Same crime. Same sentence. Same Savior in front of them.

One mocked.
“Save Yourself… and us.”

The other broke.
“Jesus… remember me.”

Same proximity.
Different posture.
And here’s the tension most people miss:

Both were guilty.
Only one went home forgiven.
But here’s what we miss…
Isaiah said it long before the nails pierced His hands:
“He was numbered with the transgressors.”

Jesus wasn’t placed there by Rome’s randomness.
He was placed there by God’s redemption plan.

Not beside saints.
Not among the righteous.
But in the middle of the guilty.

Because that’s where you are.
That’s where I am.

Caught between sin and judgment.
Breathing, but already condemned.
And Jesus steps into the center.

Not to agree with your sin.
Not to excuse it.
But to absorb it.

One criminal saw a dying man.
The other saw a King.

One died in pride.
The other died in surrender.
And in his final breath, with nothing to offer but faith…
He heard words that still shake eternity:
“Today… you will be with Me in paradise.”

No rituals.
No second chances.
No good works stacked up.
Just grace.
So why was Jesus crucified between two criminals?
Because salvation is a choice standing right beside Him.

You can reject Him…
or you can reach for Him.

Same cross.
Different ending.
You’re closer to Jesus than you think.

Say His name.
Surrender your life.
And hear what that criminal heard…
“You’re not too late.”
